text.p: Phillips Petroleum Corp said Monday commercial liquids production began April 16 from the Judy platform in the UK sector of the North Sea.
Production is currently 25,000 barrels per day (bpd) and is expected to average 35,000 to 40,0000 bpd for the rest of 1997, Phillips said.
Phillips is operator of the Judy and Joanne project, better known as the J-Block, with a 36.5 percent interest. The other owners are Agip SpA with 33 percent and BG Plc with 30.5 percent.
The natural gas produced with the liquids is being reinjected into the formation for later production and delivery to the gas buyer, Enron Corp.
The $82 million gas reinjection project is expected to increase ultimate hydrocarbon recovery from Judy and Joanne by five percent, Phillips said in a statement.

The original J-Block facilities were completed and ready for full production in February 1996, it noted. However Enron has indicated it will not take natural gas under its sales agreements until at least September of 1999.

The J-Block owners elected to reinject the gas into the formation for later production, which would enable Phillips to maintain the operational status of the facility, and produce and export the liquids. The gas reinjection facilities were installed late last year and were commissioned during the first quarter of 1997, Phillips said.

"Even with the added cost of gas reinjection equipment, the J-Block facilities were completed under budget, and the long-term economics of this project remain very favorable," the company's statement said.
It noted the Judy platform is designed to process up to 95,000 barrels per day of liquids and 450 million cubic feet per day of natural gas, of which 300 million are reserved for Enron.

With significant spare capacity in place, Phillips said, the J-Block owneres have carried out an ambitious drilling program in the area. The Jade and Jacqui field are being evaluated for future development.
